Guides

Picky eating

Being wary of new food is a normal toddler stage. Your child’s growth, not today’s plate, tells you when to ask for help.

Key points

Wariness of new foods peaks after the first birthday. A child who ate everything as a baby and gets fussier as a toddler is on a very common path. Nobody has failed.
Keep the routine, drop the negotiating. One family meal, a familiar food on the plate, and no separate dinner on request.
Ask for help when growth is the worry, not table manners. Dropping off a growth curve, fear around eating that looks like pain, or months of eating only a handful of foods is a question for a doctor.

What’s normal

Wariness of new food rises in the second year and then slowly eases. It probably helped keep children safe once they could wander off towards unknown plants. It can feel personal, but it’s mostly a developmental stage. Children also have days of eating almost nothing and days of eating loads, often in step with growth spurts rather than your menu.

A few reliable foods, sometimes called safe foods, are a real asset. Build the plate around one of them, plus some of the family meal. Don’t give up on a food for good just because it was refused twice.

What helps

Keep meals predictable. Let your child see the food without being asked to do anything with it. Eat the same food yourself. Offer refused foods cut a different way or next to a dip they like, still without comment. Fifteen quiet offers beat one big tasting showdown.

After the first birthday, milk shouldn’t take the place of meals. A toddler who drinks milk all afternoon will arrive at dinner full. Give water between meals and milk with a meal or snack, in a moderate amount over the day.

When it’s more than fussiness

Talk to your health visitor or paediatrician if weight or length gain is stalling, if eating seems to hurt, if your child coughs or vomits with certain textures, or if the list of accepted foods has shrunk to a few specific brands and keeps shrinking. More pressure won’t fix these patterns.

A child who is growing, playing, and driving you mad at dinner is usually completely ordinary. Your job is to stay calm, predictable, and available.
